design: Reward V4 — objective-dominant budget, tag economy closed, OOB farm removed
type: budget redesign, NOT a causal ablation

enemy_mav_kill_reward.rationale: The last tag payment, hidden in the offense channel: blue_kill_count = blue_tag_noflag + blue_tag_withflag + blue_mine_tags, each paid +/-0.5. Measured at 3.8x-4.2x the terminal signal in every precursor seed. The FAILED seed 2700003 ran offense +2.267 while terminal was -0.544 — out-tagging its opponents and losing. Tags remain valuable through game consequences: tagging the carrier drops the flag, tagging an attacker interrupts pressure, forcing a cooldown opens a window.

sparse_opponent_oob_points.rationale: Forcing the opponent out of bounds paid +100 — the demonstrated attractor in V3. Seed 2900002 drove red OOB 2.391x/episode for +1.903 reward/episode, 3.1x its terminal signal, while netting -17 captures and losing 89% of games. Competent seeds sat at 0.012-0.109/episode. A 195x spread is why this could never be inferred from an aggregate residual.

derivation.lambda_choice: max over NORMAL (competent) seeds; the farming seed is excluded as abnormal
derivation.check: at the p95 normal episode (1 own-OOB event) the penalty costs 0.70 reward units = 29.3% of objective reward, inside the 30% safety ceiling

sparse_mine_tag_points.reason: Mine-tag instrumentation was added AFTER V3 ran, so no V3 rate exists. A scripted probe observed 1 mine_tag event in 8 envs x 240 steps, suggestive of rarity but not a measured training rate. Per the standing rule, a term whose frequency has not been established is left unchanged and marked UNRESOLVED rather than guessed at.
sparse_mine_tag_points.note: Mine tags are paid TWICE (100 sparse + enemy_mav_kill_reward). V4 sets enemy_mav_kill_reward to 0, so their double payment is already halved as a side effect.
sparse_mine_tag_points.action: V4 measures the rate; budget it in V5 if the evidence supports it.

LEFT_UNCHANGED_DELIBERATELY.pbrs: unchanged — tests/test_pbrs_terminal.py (5 tests) demonstrated NO defect: gamma matches PPO (0.995), potentials bounded in [0,1], no terminal-step magnitude spike, no post-reset state leaking into F(s,s')

INTENT: tags matter through game consequences, not through a points faucet
forcing an opponent out of bounds is not a points farm
going out of bounds yourself remains mildly undesirable
attribution_caveat: V4 changes three reward terms at once and cannot attribute credit between them. That is deliberate: four consecutive single-term probes each improved matters and then watched the failure relocate, which is evidence of a structural budget problem rather than a single bad constant.
